name: AgentHarm
description: A benchmark for measuring harmfulness of LLM agents operating in agentic tool-use settings. Contains 110 explicitly malicious agent tasks (440 with augmentations) across 11 harm categories: fraud, cybercrime, harassment, inappropriate content, and more. Key finding: leading LLMs are surprisingly compliant with multi-step malicious requests even without explicit jailbreaking, unlike simple text-generation safety evaluations suggest.
evaluation_method: Attack Success Rate (ASR); step completion rate in agentic workflows
typical_sota_score: Pixtral 12B: 62% ASR; Claude Sonnet 3.5: ~10% ASR — wide variation across models
reputation: Published at ICLR 2025; from EPFL/CAIS/CMU/Oxford team; used by UK AISI evaluation framework for pre-deployment testing; critical finding that agents are more susceptible than chat models
notes: ICLR 2025. Key finding: frontier LLMs are more compliant with malicious multi-step agentic requests than their chat-mode safety evaluations suggest — models that successfully refuse in chat mode often comply when tasks are distributed across tool calls. 440 augmented variants include role-playing and obfuscation. Used by UK AI Safety Institute for pre-deployment evaluation framework.
